description:
checkout.commitPlace the order: obtain the user's payment approval when needed, give you an approved wallet card to enter, and submit at the order control you name.

Supply the checkout reference and the control that places the order: its reference in `submit_ref`, or a description in `submit_look` when it has none. The call pays for the terms your latest `checkout.inspect` recorded, so inspect the checkout again when its terms change. When no approval covers the terms, it shows the user the payment approval with those terms and a capture of the page, and waits for their decision. Once the user approves, the same call goes on: it gives you the wallet card, enters the Shop Pay approval, or presses the order control on the view you named it on. When the page changed meanwhile, the press is refused; observe the page and call again. The runtime reuses an approval that still covers the checkout, as described in your checkout instructions. On a card checkout, the payment approval pays with the wallet card Muse chose. With `use_wallet` and no card chosen, it lists the user's wallet cards and the user picks one. Otherwise it pays with a card entered on the page, shown as the page's payment method. An approved wallet card comes back once, with its number, expiry, security code, name and billing address, and it stays yours for this purchase: enter it again if the card fields empty. On a card-entry page before the final order control, call with `submit_ref` and `submit_look` null to get it.

It refuses until Muse has confirmed the cart. Review material changes with Muse as described in your checkout instructions. A price change alone needs no second cart confirmation; the payment approval handles any higher amount. Ask for payment approval and press the order control only through this tool. When the result says payment details were applied, continue to the final order step and call again with its order control. After a user decline, this call asks Muse how the user wants to proceed and waits for the answer. Read that answer in the result. A new call can request fresh approval from that direction; replaying the declined call keeps its refusal and the same answer. Only the merchant's confirmation proves the order went through.

username_field.description: The reference of the visible, editable username, email or phone field for the current sign-in step, from controls; null when absent, read-only or disabled, including a read-only account identifier on a password-only step.

password_field.description: The reference of the visible, editable password field for the current sign-in step, from controls; null when absent, read-only or disabled.

google_button.description: The reference of the visible Google sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

apple_button.description: The reference of the visible Apple sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

amazon_button.description: The reference of the visible Amazon sign-in control, whatever element it is, such as a button, a link or a framed button; null when the page shows none.

previous_attempt.description: What the page shows about an earlier sign-in attempt: rejected when it shows one failed, such as a wrong password message, none when it shows no earlier attempt, unknown otherwise.
